job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

response.passage: Dear Diary, today at my school in Bengaluru, our science teacher Mr. Sharma explained that everything is made of tiny particles called atoms. He told us that even a small grain of sand contains billions of atoms. I was surprised because I always thought atoms were just big, heavy things. Mr. Sharma showed us a model of a water molecule, which has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. He explained that the water molecule stays together because the atoms share a special bond. My friend Rohan asked if we could see them with our eyes. Mr. Sharma laughed and said no, because they are too small to be seen without a powerful microscope. Later, I read in my textbook that 118 different types of elements exist in nature. I spent 2 hours drawing these tiny circles in my notebook. It is amazing to think that the air I breathe and the water I drink are all built from these invisible building blocks. I feel like a scientist already, even though I am just in Class 6. I wonder if I will discover something new about them when I grow up and visit the big laboratories in Delhi.
response.summary: A student learns about atoms and molecules during a science lesson in Bengaluru. The student reflects on how these tiny, invisible particles make up everything in the world.
